blueprint.title: How Photosynthesis Supports Life
blueprint.description: A concise explanation of energy conversion and ecological importance.
blueprint.subject: Biology

sections.title: Energy Conversion in the Chloroplast
objectives: Explain how light energy becomes chemical energy

sections.title: Ecological Importance
objectives: Connect photosynthesis to food webs and atmospheric oxygen

sections.summary: Plants capture light energy and store part of it in glucose.

blocks.content: Chlorophyll in chloroplasts absorbs light, enabling plants to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose while releasing oxygen.

blocks.title: Energy pathway
blocks.caption: Light energy becomes stored chemical energy.

source_references.excerpt: Plants use light, carbon dioxide and water to make glucose and release oxygen.

sections.summary: Photosynthesis supplies biomass and oxygen that support ecosystems.

blocks.content: Because plants are producers, the chemical energy they store becomes available to organisms at higher levels of a food web.

blocks.title: Why it matters
blocks.content: Photosynthesis links solar energy, biological growth and atmospheric oxygen.

source_references.excerpt: The stored energy supports food webs, and released oxygen supports aerobic organisms.

issues_fixed: Clarified the link between producers and consumers.
